# `m.futures.contracts`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Futures contracts: the specification of every listed contract.

```python
m.futures.contracts(symbols=None, *, product_code=None, as_of=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol` and `Date` |
| `sort` | any REST field of the rows (see Massive fields below), or several separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc` |
| `filters` | `active`, `first_trade_date`, `first_trade_date_gt`, `first_trade_date_gte`, `first_trade_date_lt`, `first_trade_date_lte`, `last_trade_date`, `last_trade_date_gt`, `last_trade_date_gte`, `last_trade_date_lt`, `last_trade_date_lte`, `provider_id`, `provider_product_id`, `ticker_gt`, `ticker_gte`, `ticker_lt`, `ticker_lte`, `type`, `type_any_of` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Only these contracts; None, the default, lists every contract. `dm.ALL` is refused. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and the rows of each one you delete leave the table. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `product_code` | Only contracts of this product (`"ES"`) or these (`["ES", "NQ"]`); None for every product. A table of codes, in a `ProductCode` column, reads each code as if passed alone; a live one is followed by `fetch()` and re-read by each `poll()` cycle. |  |
| `as_of` | The day whose specifications to list; None for today. | The day to read the data as it stood on, as text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`. Leave it out for today's state. How far back you can go depends on your plan; this page's plan table says how much history each plan holds. |
| `sort` | Such as `"ticker"`; the endpoint sorts by `product_code`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | Needs `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Such as `{"active": True}` or `{"last_trade_date_gte": "2026-01-01"}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Contracts (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Futures Basic | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Starter | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Futures Developer | Updated daily, 5 years |
| Futures Advanced | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business CME | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business CBOT | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business NYMEX | Updated daily, All history |
| Futures Business COMEX | Updated daily, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `ticker`: "The ticker for the contract." | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `Active` | boolean | Whether or not a given contract was tradeable at the given point in time. Active is true when (first_trade_date <= date <= last_trade_date) and false otherwise. | REST |
| `Date` | String | The day, YYYY-MM-DD, whose point-in-time state the row describes: whether the contract was tradeable that day (`active`) and its days to maturity from it. | REST |
| `DaysToMaturity` | long | The number of calendar days between the 'date' and the contract's final settlement date. | REST |
| `FirstTradeDate` | String | The first day on which the contract was tradeable. | REST |
| `GroupCode` | String | An identifier used to identify logical groups of products. The group_code is only populated for contracts listed for trading on CME Globex. | REST |
| `LastTradeDate` | String | The last day on which the contract was tradeable. | REST |
| `MaxOrderQuantity` | long | The maximum order quantity. | REST |
| `MinOrderQuantity` | long | The minimum order quantity. | REST |
| `Name` | String | The name of this contract. | REST |
| `ProductCode` | String | The identifier for the contract's product. | REST |
| `ProviderId` | String | A unique identifier for the contract assigned by the data provider. Note that this value is null for historical data (pre-2025-03-12). | REST |
| `ProviderProductId` | String | A unique identifier for the product to which a contract, or contracts, belongs. Note that this value is null for historical data (pre-2025-03-12). | REST |
| `SettlementDate` | String | The date on which this contract settles. | REST |
| `SettlementTickSize` | double | The tick size for settlement. | REST |
| `SpreadTickSize` | double | The tick size for spreads. | REST |
| `TradeTickSize` | double | The tick size for trades. | REST |
| `TradingVenue` | String | The trading venue (MIC) for the exchange on which this contract trades. | REST |
| `Type` | String | The type of contract, one of 'single' or 'combo'. Leaving this filter blank will query for contracts where type is 'single', 'combo' or empty. This field only exists on contracts as of 2025-03-12 and later. It will be null when date < 2025-03-12. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
